name: Gufic Biosciences Ltd
title: Gufic Biosciences Ltd - 509079 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Gufic Q1 FY27 revenue rose 15% YoY to INR260.8 crore and PAT rose 86% to INR22.5 crore, with EBITDA margin at 18.09%.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR260.8 crore versus INR226.9 crore a year earlier and INR252.1 crore in Q4 FY26. EBITDA rose to INR47.2 crore (18.09% margin) from INR33.2 crore (14.6%), and PAT reached INR22.46 crore (8.61% margin) versus INR12.1 crore. Management said Indore is running to plan, with capacity utilisation expected to reach 40-45% by year-end and the GLP-1 CMO ramp expected to build from Q2 and more in Q3. Management reiterated 15-20% annual growth as a minimum commitment, with EU and US certifications for Indore still pending.

segments.name: Critical Care
segments.commentary: Launched monobactam and beta-lactamase inhibitor combination on innovator patent expiry; Sparsh completed a full quarter on the rebuilt channel with outstanding days within trade terms. Focus is on own-manufactured brands and depth within existing hospital groups.

segments.name: Women's health / IVF (Puregraf, Ferticare, Zenova)
segments.commentary: Ferticare retains leadership in recurrent implantation failure; Puregraf entered major corporate IVF chains. Zenova is shifting from injectables to prescription chronic therapies, with two first-mover launches (osteoarthritis, metabolic ovarian) due ahead.

segments.name: Aesthetics (botulinum toxin and fillers)
segments.commentary: Claims to be number 2 in toxin type A in India, made from its own strain. Filler partnership with Revanesse (Prollenium, Canada) expected to launch in India around December-January, subject to registration in Q2 or mid-Q3.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Shifted to a model that earns fee income alongside supply revenue. Licensing progressed in Europe, a contract manufacturing and licensing arrangement was signed with a North American partner, and first CMO orders were received in Australia. Approvals were secured in 8 countries in the quarter.

segments.name: GLP-1 (semaglutide, via Hetero)
segments.commentary: Operates purely as a CMO for Hetero, which received permission in May 2026; Q1 revenue contribution was residual. A 10-15 day plant shutdown in Q1 was for a new machine. Management expects traction from Q2 and the main contribution in Q3, with 70% of capacity targeted for international use.

guidance_outlook: Management commits to 15-20% year-on-year company growth as a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond that.
Indore capacity utilisation expected to rise from about 30-35% now to around 40-45% by year-end, with the Indore liquid line targeted at about 80% utilisation within three years.
Margin expansion from Indore expected once EU certification is in place. Management says the 18% operating margin is the start of an improvement trend, not a new normal.
Management expects operating leverage to start around mid-FY28.

Indore revenue potential is INR800-1,200 crore from current capex (about INR300 crore), so combined with Navsari the maximum is about INR1,600-2,000 crore; management also cited INR1,600-1,800 crore with no further capex.
Botulinum toxin and biostimulator in-licensed products are to launch this financial year with no significant capex. Stunnox and Zarbot registrations in SE Asia and Africa take 12-18 months.
capex_capacity: Indore has about 6 lyophilisers (4 at 100,000-vial capacity and 2 at 44,000-vial capacity). Depot and liposomal lines are in installation and qualification, with both targeted to be operational this year.
Indore has four lines: two lyophilisation lines, one suspension/liquid vial line, and one ampoule line. Target mix is roughly 20% liquid, 50-60% lyophilisation, and 20-30% complex injectables.
Indore is fully operational as a unit; new product lines are being added within the existing capex of about INR300 crore, with no major new infrastructure.
Indore utilisation has risen from 18-22% last year, to 20-25%, to close to 30-35% this year.
Navsari is largely capped at about INR800 crore revenue, with toxin and penem blocks not yet saturated.
Toxin plant is WHO Phase 1 with limited capacity; global registrations are deferred until after next year pending cash flow.
demand_pricing: Average revenue per vial is about INR80-100 on current product mix (pantoprazole 10 ml vial at about INR60-80). Management aims to move to INR300-400 and eventually an average of INR500 per vial with depot, liposomal and complex injectables.
Fillers market in India is estimated at about INR200 crore. Management aims to move from number 2 to number 1 in toxin plus fillers within 3-5 years.

International: aims to raise margins from 40-50% under distributor models to 15-20% higher with its own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia. Recruitment of a regional team happened in Q1.
CHAI partnership for liposomal amphotericin B gives access to more than 100 markets; bioequivalence study due by August-September, followed by WHO PQ filing.

Employee additions are mainly at Indore (around 50-60 for domestic expansion), with international headcount capped at 20-25. Management says the previous-year contract-to-payroll conversion was one-time.

qa_highlights.question: Is Gufic participating in GLP-1 (semaglutide) under its own brand, and has third-party CMO revenue started?
qa_highlights.answer: Pranav Choksi said GLP-1 is purely a CMO role for Hetero, which got permission in May 2026, so Q1 revenue was residual. CMO traction is expected to build from Q2, with the main contribution in Q3; about 30% of capacity is for domestic CMO and about 70% for international use, where Hetero and Gufic have filed in more than 22 countries. No front-end role is planned in India or abroad.

qa_highlights.question: How does the shift in international model (distributor-led to own-registration, field-force led) change economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is moving to own field force in Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia once registrations and scale allow, aiming to lift margins from 40-50% under distributor models by 15-20% or more. A regional team was recruited in Q1 (one person in Mexico, one in the Philippines, two in Mumbai); the company also says it is building IP and trademarks in these markets.

qa_highlights.question: When will Indore get EU certification and does margin expansion follow, and is 18% the new normal margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Navsari already holds EU certification. The Indore EU certificate is awaited, with feedback expected in about one to two months; a US partner has also filed from the site. Indore utilisation was 18-22% last year, 20-25% the year before, and close to 30-35% this year, targeted at 40-45% by year-end. Management said the 18% margin is the start of an improvement trend rather than a new normal, and that the earlier 18% period had Indore costs, depreciation and interest capitalised.

qa_highlights.question: Will Fillers (Revanesse tie-up) scale, and how big is the opportunity?
qa_highlights.answer: The Indian filler market is estimated at about INR200 crore. Launch is expected around December-January, after registration in Q2 or mid-Q3. Management gave no first-year revenue number and aims to move from number 2 to number 1 in toxin plus fillers within 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15-20% growth conservative, and can growth go beyond 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15-20% year-on-year company growth is a bare minimum, with efforts aimed at growing beyond it. Some low-yielding product mix is being squeezed out, and it was not conservative in that guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak revenue potential from current capacity without further capex (analyst cited about INR2,700 crore)?
qa_highlights.answer: Roonghta first put FY27 expected revenue at about INR1,100 crore, with 15% annual growth taking it to about INR1,600 crore on existing facilities. Pranav Choksi said Navsari is capped at about INR800 crore, with toxin and penem not saturated, and Indore could add INR800-1,200 crore on about INR300 crore capex. The combined no-capex figure was cited as INR1,600-1,800 crore, and the total maximum as INR1,600-2,000 crore. The INR2,700 crore figure was not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: What is the planned employee addition strategy, and what productivity metrics are used?
qa_highlights.answer: Most additions are at Indore, with about 50-60 people for domestic expansion, while international headcount is capped at 20-25. The previous year's increase reflected contract staff moving to payroll in Indore and Navsari for quality roles, which management called a one-time step. Employee cost growth is in line with the company's overall growth.

qa_highlights.question: When will operating leverage from Indore's product mix start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects operating leverage to start around mid-FY28. Indore has 6 lyophilisers (4 at 100,000-vial and 2 at 44,000-vial capacity). Target mix is about 20% liquid, 50-60% lyophilisation and 20-30% complex injectables, with the liquid line targeted at about 80% utilisation within 3 years.

risks_watch: Indore EU certification is still pending, and margin expansion depends on it; the US partner audit timing is also uncertain.
GLP-1 CMO ramp is back-ended (Q2 traction, Q3 main contribution) and depends on Hetero's approvals; a 5-day plant shutdown is planned for visits.
Average realisation per vial is INR80-100 today; the INR300-500 per vial target depends on depot, liposomal and complex injectables launching on schedule.
Toxin plant is WHO Phase 1 with limited capacity; global registrations are deferred to after next year pending cash flow.
Filler launch (Revanesse) timing depends on registration in Q2 or mid-Q3; first-year revenue was not quantified.
Management's peak revenue figures were inconsistent during the call (INR1,600 crore, INR1,600-1,800 crore, INR1,600-2,000 crore), so the capacity-revenue framework needs clarification.
Rising employee count, with 50-60 domestic and 20-25 international additions, needs productivity tracking against operating leverage.

But 15% to 20% is what we commit to you that would be a bare minimum.

summary.management_tone: Confident on Indore's operational progress, the 15-20% growth floor and the margin trajectory, but cautious on timelines, deferring the EU certificate, global toxin registrations and any margin uplift from exports until approvals come through. Answers on revenue capacity were less precise and at times reconciled on the fly.
